samples.summary: Gate 1b's CI_DEFINING_PATHS omits the per-package build/test/lint configs that actually decide what each CI lane runs (`packages/*/vite.config.ts`, `packages/*/vitest.config.ts`, `packages/*/tsconfig.json`, `packages/*/eslint.config.*`, root `eslint.config.mjs`, `.npmrc`), so a branch can neutralise CI and still auto-promote
samples.evidence: The new gate refuses promotion only when a changed path matches CI_DEFINING_PATHS (checks.mjs:123-135, enforced at mark-ready.mjs:217). `packages/*/package.json` is on the list with the stated reason "a package's own test/typecheck script is what verify:self invokes for that package, so editing it edits a lane" — but the script it invokes is `vitest --run` / `tsc --noEmit`, and *those* read files that are NOT on the list. This is not the residue the module documents (checks.mjs:116-121 concedes only "a branch can always edit its own test files"); a vitest/tsconfig/eslint config is lane configuration, the same category as the per-package `package.json` the list does include. samples.summary: The new producer guard on capture-collect.yml is bypassable: the nightly `schedule` sweep runs the same job with the same `secrets.EVAL_STORE_TOKEN`, and the collector selects artifacts repo-wide by NAME PREFIX with no check on the producing workflow, so a forged (or fork-PR) run's artifact is still committed to the other repository
samples.evidence: capture-collect.yml:138-144 now admits `workflow_run` only from `.github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml` / `agent-review-on-demand.yml` in this repo, and the comment justifies it as keeping a forged `name: Agent Review Panel` run away from "secrets.EVAL_STORE_TOKEN, a write PAT for ANOTHER repository". But the first disjunct `github.event_name != 'workflow_run'` admits every `schedule` run (cron at capture-collect.yml:75), and that run executes the identical steps with the identical PAT (capture-collect.yml:157-161). What it collects is decided by scripts/agent/collect-captures.mjs:436-446: `planCollection` walks the repository-wide artifact listing and keeps anything whose name starts with `review-panel-stage-detail` — `a.workflow_run` is read only for its `id` (line 450), never to check which workflow file produced the run. A push that lands between the re-read and the flip leaves the PR promoted to "ready for human review", with the hand-off comment at lines 403-419 asserting CI green and panel approval "for this exact head SHA", for a commit that neither gate ever saw. `gh pr ready` takes no expected-SHA, so the correct closing move is a final head re-read immediately before the mutation (and after gate 2's read), not one in the middle of the gate chain. verdict.reason: Verified in the repo. capture-collect.yml:138-144 gates only `workflow_run` (first disjunct `github.event_name != 'workflow_run'` lets `schedule` (cron, line 74-75) and `workflow_dispatch` (line 88) through), while the scheduled run performs the identical checkout of dlgpdmsly2/wafflebase-agent-eval with secrets.EVAL_STORE_TOKEN (lines 157-161) and pushes (line 273). verdict.reason: Verified independently: CI_DEFINING_PATHS (checks.mjs:123-135) has no entry that can match `scripts/failure-summary.mjs` or `scripts/agent/git-env.mjs` (the regex builder at checks.mjs:140-153 anchors both ends and `*` does not cross separators), yet scripts/verify-self.mjs:2-3 imports both at module scope, and package.json:25 + ci.yml:308 make verify-self.mjs the entry point the rest of CI gates on (ci.yml:371/438/553). The omission is deliberate, not accidental: checks.test.mjs:537-548 asserts definesCi("scripts/agent/checks.mjs") === false, so the whole scripts/agent tree is outside the refusal surface, and the mirror test (checks.test.mjs:492-512) only demands a superset of harness.config.json:52-62's ciConfig, which lists neither path. Consumer chain matches the claim: ciDefiningPathsChanged (mark-ready.mjs:205-226) filters pulls/N/files through definesCi, ranBaseCiDefinition (mark-ready.mjs:236-273) returns true on zero hits, and mark-ready.mjs:406-411 then tells the accountable human signer that "the CI definition that run executed came from `main` rather than from the branch" — false for a branch that added a top-level side effect (e.g. process.exit(0)) to scripts/failure-summary.mjs, since ESM evaluates it before verify-self.mjs's body and the lane exits 0 having run nothing. I searched for a counterexample and found none: definesCi/CI_DEFINING_PATHS have exactly two consumers repo-wide (mark-ready.mjs:217 and the tests), there is no transitive-import check over scripts/verify-*.mjs, the promote job (agent-review-panel.yml:1453-1550) adds no path check, and no ci.yml step after line 308 re-validates that lanes executed (the .harness-reports upload at ci.yml:360-367 is if: always()). .github/CODEOWNERS:32 owns /scripts/agent/ but not scripts/failure-summary.mjs, applies only at merge time and only if the branch-protection option is enabled (its own lines 22-26), and does not participate in gate 1b or in the truth of the hand-off comment — so it is not an "already-guarded" refutation. Blocking under the security lens as a bypassable integrity/authorization gate whose bypass produces a false attestation to the human signer.

mergedFrom.summary: The change enumerates every display-name-triggered `workflow_run` consumer and omits capture-collect.yml, which is triggered by display name and holds a cross-repo push secret

finding.summary: `capture-collect.yml` is the same forgery class the change hardens elsewhere and got no `path` clause: it consumes `workflow_run` by display name with no path / branch / head-repository guard while holding a cross-repo write PAT
finding.evidence:
This change adds `github.event.workflow_run.path == '.github/workflows/ci.yml'` to agent-review-panel.yml, agent-iterate-ci.yml and ci-report.yml, and checks.test.mjs's new "every workflow_run consumer" test enumerates exactly those three. capture-collect.yml consumes the same event class and is left open:

  line 67-69: `workflow_run: workflows: ["Agent Review Panel", "Agent Review On-Demand"]` — display names, which the diff's own reasoning establishes are only a `name:` key and are not unique.
  line 129: `if: ${{ github.event_name != 'workflow_run' || github.event.workflow_run.conclusion != 'skipped' }}` — the only gate. No `path`, no `head_branch`, no `head_repository.full_name == github.repository`.
  line 142-146: `actions/checkout` of `dlgpdmsly2/wafflebase-agent-eval` with `token: ${{ secrets.EVAL_STORE_TOKEN }}` (documented at line 20-23 as a fine-grained PAT with `Contents: read and write` on that repo).
  line 220-259: `git commit` + `git push` with those persisted credentials.

So anyone able to land a workflow file on a branch named `name: Agent Review Panel` can drive a job that pushes to a second repository using a PAT this repository's read-only `permissions:` block otherwise deliberately withholds. It also lets a forged run repeatedly occupy the `capture-collect` concurrency group (line 109-111, `cancel-in-progress: false`), queueing out real collections. The docs added in this change (docs/design/harness-engineering.md, docs/tasks/active/20260825-…-todo.md item 1) acknowledge the gap and defer it to a maintainer, so this is a known-and-recorded exposure rather than an oversight — but the guard is still absent and the new test that would have pinned it is written to take a (file, job) pair and simply does not list this file.

verdict.reason: The finding claims capture-collect.yml's only workflow_run gate is a lone `conclusion != 'skipped'` check with no path/head-repository guard. In the working tree the job's `if:` at .github/workflows/capture-collect.yml:138-144 contains all three clauses: `conclusion != 'skipped'`, `head_repository.full_name == github.repository`, and a `path` disjunction pinning `.github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml` or `.github/workflows/agent-review-on-demand.yml`. That gate sits on the same job that checks out dlgpdmsly2/wafflebase-agent-eval with secrets.EVAL_STORE_TOKEN (line 157-161) and pushes (line 273), so a forged `name: Agent Review Panel` file cannot reach the PAT — its payload `path` fails the disjunction — and the concurrency-occupancy variant is closed by the same expression, while schedule/dispatch still pass via the `event_name != 'workflow_run'` short-circuit. The second half of the claim is also wrong: scripts/agent/checks.test.mjs:606-651 is a dedicated block in the same "every workflow_run consumer" test that extracts capture-collect's `if:` and asserts a forged file (line 640-642), a fork (line 643-646) and an absent path (line 647-649) are all refused. The reviewer looked only at the (file, job) loop preceding it.

searchedFor: Grep 'create-github-app-token' with 8 lines of context across .github/workflows

finding.summary: The fixer arm this change hardens still mints a full-installation App token from a mutable `@v1` tag and hands it to a job that checks out and executes untrusted branch code
finding.evidence:
agent-iterate-ci.yml:104-115:

  - name: Generate GitHub App token
    id: app-token
    uses: actions/create-github-app-token@v1        # mutable tag, handles AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY
    with:
      app-id: ${{ secrets.AGENT_APP_ID }}
      private-key: ${{ secrets.AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
                                                    # <- no permission-* inputs at all
  - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    with:
      ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_branch }}
      token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}

Two defects in one step. (a) Unpinned: every other consumer in this repo pins `@d72941d797fd3113feb6b93fd0dec494b13a2547 # v1.12.0` and says why (agent-review-panel.yml:1485-1488 "Pinned to an immutable commit SHA (not the movable @v1 tag) for supply-chain safety — this action handles the App private key"). A compromised or retagged `v1` sees `AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`, i.e. the whole installation, not one token. (b) Unscoped: with no `permission-*` inputs the minted token carries every permission the installation holds — compare agent-fix.yml:121-129 and agent-review-panel.yml:1800-1808, which scope theirs precisely because "this token is live in a job that later checks out and executes untrusted branch code", which is exactly what happens on the next line here (the fixer agent installs, builds and tests the PR branch).

This is directly coupled to the change under review: the diff's justification for the new `path` clause is that a forged `name: CI` run "would otherwise drive this workflow's `contents: write` fixer". Closing the trigger while the token stays full-installation and mutable-tagged leaves the larger half of that arm's blast radius intact. Same pattern at agent-implement.yml:119 and agent-review-reply.yml:126. Recorded as maintainer work in docs/tasks/active/20260825-…-todo.md item 2, but still present in the tree.

verdict.reason: Both halves of the finding are present verbatim. agent-iterate-ci.yml:106 uses the mutable `actions/create-github-app-token@v1` tag while handing it AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY (line 109), and supplies no `permission-*` inputs, so the minted token inherits the App installation's full permission set. This deviates from the repo's own documented control: 9 of 12 call sites pin the immutable SHA d72941d797fd3113feb6b93fd0dec494b13a2547 # v1.12.0 (agent-fix.yml:121, agent-review-panel.yml:1488/1800) with comments stating the pin exists "for supply-chain safety - this action handles the App private key", and agent-fix.yml:125-130 / agent-review-panel.yml:1804-1810 scope their tokens precisely because "this token is live in a job that later checks out and executes untrusted branch code". That condition holds here: the token is consumed at agent-iterate-ci.yml:111-115 by actions/checkout with no `persist-credentials: false` (unlike the trusted-main checkout at line 142), writing a full-installation credential into the workspace .git/config, after which the job runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` on branch-controlled lockfile/postinstall (line 285) and a fixer agent with Bash/Write (line 430); the token is also in step env at lines 375, 463, 523. No guard makes it unreachable: the `path == '.github/workflows/ci.yml'` trigger check (line 54) and fork exclusion (line 56) gate who triggers the job, but managed base-repo branches (lines 76-80) reach it by design. Secrets exposure and least-privilege on a credential reachable by untrusted code are in the security lane; the pending todo entry does not discharge it.

finding.summary: The author/fixer paths mint an UNSCOPED GitHub App installation token from a mutable action tag, which is what makes the gate-2 forgery above reachable
finding.evidence: agent-implement.yml:117-122 and agent-iterate-ci.yml:104-109 call `actions/create-github-app-token@v1` with `app-id`/`private-key` and NO `permission-*` inputs, so the minted token carries every permission the installation holds — handed to a job that then executes model-directed code with the branch checked out. Every other consumer in this repo scopes the token explicitly and pins the action to an immutable SHA for exactly this reason: agent-review-panel.yml:1483-1493 ("Pinned to an immutable commit SHA (not the movable @v1 tag) for supply-chain safety — this action handles the App private key", plus `permission-pull-requests: write` / `permission-issues: write`), agent-rerun.yml:94-98, agent-loop.yml:83-87, ci-report.yml:86-94. Two consequences: (1) if the installation carries `Checks: write`, the unscoped token lets the author agent post its own `agent-review-*` check runs, which `checkPassed` accepts because it never checks `app.slug` — that is the gate-2 bypass reported separately; (2) a compromised or retagged `@v1` reads `secrets.AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`. Pre-existing and outside the diff, but the diff's whole premise is that these gates are unforgeable, and the token scope is what decides that.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo: agent-implement.yml:117-122 and agent-iterate-ci.yml:104-109 both call actions/create-github-app-token@v1 (mutable tag) with only app-id/private-key and NO permission-* inputs, so the minted token carries the App installation's full permission set. That token is then passed to actions/checkout (agent-implement.yml:200; agent-iterate-ci.yml:115, checking out the attacker-influenceable head_branch) in a job that installs deps and executes model-directed agent code — the exact posture the repo's own sibling workflows document as the reason for least privilege (agent-fix.yml:125-129, agent-review-panel.yml:1804-1808). Every other consumer pins the immutable SHA d72941d797fd3113feb6b93fd0dec494b13a2547 AND scopes permission-* (agent-loop.yml:83-87, agent-rerun.yml:94-98, ci-report.yml:86-94, agent-summarize.yml:116-120, agent-review-on-demand.yml:112-116, agent-review-panel.yml:1488-1493); a third unscoped @v1 instance also exists at agent-review-reply.yml:126. Consequence (2) — a retagged or compromised @v1 reads secrets.AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY — is valid on its face. One sub-claim IS wrong: checkPassed does verify app.slug (scripts/agent/checks.mjs:265-272 filters on r?.app?.slug === CHECK_PRODUCER_APP_SLUG, with tests at checks.test.mjs:57-81), which undercuts the gate-2 forgery chain in consequence (1). But that is only one of two stated consequences and does not touch the independently real weakness: an unscoped, unpinned installation token exposed to untrusted and model-directed code. That is secrets/privilege-scope exposure, squarely in the security lane, and blocking at major severity.
